about: Part of the reference catalogue: worked examples, designs and exercises with data from chapters 1 and 2 of
Montgomery, Design and Analysis of Experiments (8th edition), for testing that software reproduces them. source:
the citation, with what was read and when. experiments: each worked example or exercise with data (factors,
responses, runs exactly as printed, in the printed order), where it is printed, and expected: every number the
book prints for it, as printed text, with where it is printed (a page and a quotation) and check: how to
recompute it, or manual, the reason it is not recomputed. A check with a disagreement records a number known not
to reproduce and why. A two-group comparison is checked with the library's t-tests (t_test, runs less minus) and,
where the two agree by construction, with the regression on the group coded -1 and +1, or with the randomized
block model for a paired comparison. design.treatment_factors counts the factors varied as treatments, blocks not
counted: 0 for a single sample. An exercise the book does not answer is marked unanswered and its runs are kept
as data. designs: the run counts and the half fraction the book states in chapter 1. not_captured: what in these
pages is not an experiment with data. Read with process_improve.experiments.reference_catalogue.
reference_experiments; tests/test_reference_catalogue.py recomputes every number that has a check.

experiments.name: montgomery-portland-cement
experiments.title: Tension bond strength of Portland cement mortar, modified with a polymer latex emulsion and unmodified

factors.description: mortar formulation: modified, with a polymer latex emulsion added during mixing, or the original unmodified

design.details: 10 samples of the modified and 10 of the unmodified formulation

experiments.notes: The book and Minitab take the difference as modified less unmodified, ȳ1 − ȳ2; JMP takes unmodified less modified. The pooled two-sample t-test is the regression of strength on the formulation coded −1 and +1: the effect is the difference of the two averages and its t is the test's. Each of the test's numbers is therefore checked twice, with the library's t-test (univariate.metrics.ttest_independent) and with analyze_experiment. The powers of section 2.4.3 are the library's power for the coefficient of a two-level factor in a design of n runs at each level: an effect of δ is a coefficient of δ/2.
